slide-01.alt: Trust at the speed of AI. Kujo makes agent-driven engineering work inspectable, repeatable and accountable across existing workflows.

slide-02.alt: Software production is outpacing verification. Agents can report completion. Teams still need a reviewable chain from requested work to release decision.

slide-03.alt: Agents now work across the repository. GitHub documents agents that plan changes, edit code and review pull requests. More delegated work makes the execution record part of the review.

slide-04.alt: A passing summary can hide a failed checkout. A coupon changes a $50 cart to $50.99 instead of $45. The reviewer needs the failing test, exact change and unchanged checks.

slide-05.alt: Build with clarity. Operate with control. The language is the long-term foundation. Existing tools offer an earlier route into engineering workflows.

slide-06.alt: Accountability spans the whole task. Each component owns a specific responsibility. A reviewable workflow composes their artifacts explicitly.

slide-07.alt: A working foundation precedes this raise. The language, execution tools and integration adapters are inspectable in public source.

slide-08.alt: Keep the failure. Verify the correction. A reproducible checkout regression: a coupon must preserve free shipping. The original tests fail, a one-line correction passes them.

slide-09.alt: Adopt the ecosystem before the language. Keep application code in its existing language. Introduce accountability at the workflow boundary.

slide-10.alt: Start with the platform engineering lead. Initial buyer hypothesis: a team operating coding agents across repositories and reconstructing failures during review.

slide-11.alt: Open tools today. A team service to validate. Primary paid wedge: shared agent-run evidence and review for engineering teams. Application code stays in its existing language.

slide-12.alt: A clear path from team adoption to recurring revenue. One team subscription at $500 per month. Scale revenue through retained teams and repeatable adoption.

slide-13.alt: Portable evidence across existing workflows. GitHub integrates agents and review. LangGraph persists workflow state. Kujo composes local execution artifacts with explicit evaluation.

slide-14.alt: Turn a first evidence run into a retained team. Integration-led distribution: one useful repository workflow, then a buyer conversation about shared review.

slide-15.alt: Public engineering and distribution are visible. Technical momentum is independently inspectable. Commercial validation is the next milestone.

slide-16.alt: A founder with a public shipping record. Robert DeVore builds commercial web software and the Kujo language ecosystem.

slide-17.alt: Fund commercialization with staged commitments. Proposed $6M raise: a 24-month operating plan with $900K reserve. Release hiring against validation, paid pilots and retention.

slide-18.alt: Help build the accountability layer for AI. $6M to bring Kujo’s agent evidence and review platform to engineering teams.
